description.narrative: International Budget Partnership (IBP) har ansökt om stöd från Sida om totalt 5 000 000 SEK för att genomföra IBP landstrategi för Kenya med fokus på budgettransparens 2013-2015. Insatsen syftar till att öka efterfrågan på transparens av statsbudgeten, och användandet av budgetanalyser i offentliga debatter, öka utbudet av budgetinformation, förbättra budgettransparensen på länsnivå och stödja transitionsprocessen till ett decentraliserat system. Den totala budgeten för 2013-2015 är 1 741 215 USD av vilket Sida finansierar 699 660 USD, Gates foundation 955 880 USD och Omidyar 85 675 USD.

The International Budget Partnership (IBP) has requested for support from Sida totalling 5 000 000 SEK for the implementation of its Kenya Strategy 2013-2015 focusing on budget transparency. The purpose is to increase the demand for transparency of the state budget, increase the use of budget analysis in public debate, increase the supply fo budget information, improve the budget transparency at county level and support the devolution process. The total budget 2013-2015 is 1 714 215 USD of which Sida finances 699 660 USD, Gates Foundation 955 880 USD and Omidyar 85 675 USD.

General question: Results related to the intended outcome 2016Question: Summarise results related to the intended outcome (this information will be sent to Open Aid)Answer: IBP Kenya is increasingly recognized as an anchor institution, which is good but also implies a heavy burden. IBPK has built new partnerships during this period, founded on mutual interest and respect, though older partnerships have not always proved robust. The work on county budgets is a long-term activity and the choice of using more adaptive strategy has allowed IBPK to find promising opportunities in a number of counties. While working with individual “model” counties has not been successful, IBPK has been able to continue to build up their network of county Heads of Budget, which formed a stronger steering committee toward the end of 2016 and has committed to more aggressive action in 2017. Working with government in particular the National Treasury and the Controller of Budget, remains a challenging area where there has been both success and failure throughout the project period. Some successful collaboration with the Office of the Auditor General, has taken place with the OAG having been quite open to CSO engagement and has worked with IBPK, GIZ and PIN on various activities, including discussions around improving audit reports, simplifying them, and engaging better with media. Relationships with some county officials such as the Heads of Budget have also been constructive.
